  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:LoansNotesTradeAndOtherReceivablesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3166298" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;">Commercial loans are divided among <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> segments based primarily on collateral type, risk characteristics, and primary and secondary sources of repayment. These segments are then further stratified based on the commercial loan grade that is assigned using our standard loan grading paradigm. Retail loans are divided into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> groups based on risk characteristics and source of repayment. Our allowance for credit loss pools are consistent with those used for loan note disclosure purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt;">Our loan portfolio segments as of both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, were as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 9pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">o</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Commercial Loans</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 69px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 17px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1573px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Commercial and Industrial</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the practical limitations associated with monitoring the condition of the collateral which often consists of inventory, accounts receivable, and other non-real estate assets. Equipment and inventory obsolescence can also pose a risk. Declines in general economic conditions and other events can cause cash flows to fall to levels insufficient to service debt.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 70px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 15px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1574px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Owner Occupied Commercial Real Estate</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the inability to monitor the condition of the collateral. Declines in general economic conditions and other events can cause cash flows to fall to levels insufficient to service debt. Also, declines in real estate values and lack of suitable alternative uses for the properties are risks for loans in this category.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 71px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 15px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1574px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Non-Owner Occupied Commercial Real Estate</span>: Loans in this category are susceptible to declines in occupancy rates, business failure, and general economic conditions. Also, declines in real estate values and lack of suitable alternative uses for the properties are risks for loans in this category.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 72px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 15px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1572px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Multi-Family and Residential Rental</span>: Risks to this loan category include industry concentration and the inability to monitor the condition of the collateral. Loans in this category are susceptible to weakening general economic conditions and increases in unemployment rates, as well as market demand and supply of similar property and the resulting impact on occupancy rates, market rents, cash flow, and income-based real estate values. Also, the lack of suitable alternative uses for the properties is a risk for loans in this category.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 71px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 16px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1572px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Vacant Land, Land Development and Residential Construction</span>: Risks common to commercial construction loans are cost overruns, changes in market demand for property, inadequate long-term financing arrangements, and declines in real estate values. Residential construction loans are susceptible to those same risks as well as those associated with residential mortgage loans. Changes in market demand for property could lead to longer marketing times resulting in higher carrying costs, declining values, and higher interest rates.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 9pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">o</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">Retail Loans</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 73px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 14px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1572px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; "><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> Family Mortgages</span>: Residential mortgage loans are susceptible to weakening general economic conditions and increases in unemployment rates and declining real estate values.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 73px;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 12px;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9632;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: middle; width: 1574px;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Other Consumer Loans</span>: Risks common to these loans include regulatory risks, unemployment, and changes in local economic conditions as well as the inability to monitor collateral consisting of personal property.</p></td></tr>
</tbody></table><ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Our total loans at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, were $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706296" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">4.82</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion, a&#160;decrease of $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706297" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:IncreaseDecreaseInFinanceReceivables" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">5.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, or <ix:nonFraction id="c143706298" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:LoansAndLeasesReceivablePercentagePeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3" sign="-">0.1</ix:nonFraction>%, compared to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. The components of our loan portfolio disaggregated by class of loan within the loan portfolio segments at <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and the percentage change in loans from the end of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> to the end of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>, are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfAccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableTextBlock" id="c3166299" escape="true">
    <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="finTable" style="width: 95%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; text-indent: 0px; margin-left: 18pt; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr class="finHeading" style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;">Nonaccrual loans represent the entire balance of collateral dependent loans. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, all collateral dependent loans were secured by real estate, with the exception of those classified as commercial and industrial, which were secured by accounts receivable, inventory, and equipment.&#160;Interest income recognized on nonaccrual loans totaled&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143706306" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c143706307" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableNonaccrualInterestIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively,&#160;reflecting the collection of interest at the time of principal pay off.&#160;</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</span></b> (Continued)</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Credit Quality Indicators. </i>We utilize a comprehensive grading system for our commercial loans. All commercial loans are graded on a <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> grade rating system. The rating system utilizes standardized grade paradigms that analyze several critical factors such as cash flow, operating performance, financial condition, collateral, industry condition and management. All commercial loans are graded at inception and reviewed and, if appropriate, re-graded at various intervals thereafter. The primary risk elements with respect to commercial loans are the financial condition of the borrower, sufficiency of collateral, and timeliness of scheduled payments. We have a policy of requesting and reviewing periodic financial statements from commercial loan customers and employ a disciplined and formalized review of the existence of collateral and its value. All commercial loans are graded using the following criteria:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; width: 95%; margin-left: 18pt; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Exceptional&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating contain very little, if any, risk.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Outstanding&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have excellent and stable sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Very Good&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have strong sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements. These are loans for which repayment risks are acceptable.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">4.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Good&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have solid sources of repayment and conform to bank policy and regulatory requirements. These are loans for which repayment risks are modest.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Acceptable&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating exhibit acceptable sources of repayment and conform with most bank policies and all regulatory requirements. These are&#160;loans for which repayment risks are satisfactory.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Monitor&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating are considered to have emerging weaknesses which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include negative current cash flow, high leverage, or operating losses. Generally, if further deterioration is observed, these credits will be downgraded to the criticized asset report.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Special Mention&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating have potential weaknesses that deserve management&#8217;s close attention. If left uncorrected, these potential weaknesses <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in deterioration of the repayment prospects for the loan at some future date.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">8.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Substandard&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating&#160;are inadequately protected by current sound net worth, paying capacity of the obligor, or of the pledged collateral, if any. A Substandard loan normally has <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more well-defined weaknesses that jeopardize the repayment of the debt. They are characterized by the distinct possibility of loss if the deficiencies are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">9.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Doubtful&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating exhibit all the weaknesses inherent in the Substandard classification and where collection or liquidation in full is highly questionable and improbable.</p> </td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 10%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Grade <em style="font: inherit;">10.</em></p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; width: 90%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#8220;Loss&#8221;&#160;&#160;Loans with this rating are considered uncollectable, and of such little value that continuance as an active asset is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> warranted.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&#160;</p>
   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; width: 95%; margin-left: 18pt; margin-right: auto;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td colspan="2" style="vertical-align: top; width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">The primary risk element with respect to each residential real estate loan and consumer loan is the timeliness of scheduled payments. We have a reporting system that monitors past due loans and have adopted policies to pursue creditors&#8217;&#160;rights in order to preserve our collateral position. Retail loans that reach <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days or more past due are generally placed into nonaccrual status and are categorized as nonperforming.</p></td></tr>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">LOANS AND ALLOWANCE FOR CREDIT LOSSES</span></b> (Continued)</p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">We use a migration to loss methodology to determine historical loss rates for commercial loans given the comprehensive loan grading process employed by Mercantile for over <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> decades, while an open pool approach is best suited for retail loans given the smaller dollar size of the segments. A baseline loss rate is produced at each reporting date for each loan portfolio segment using bank-specific loan charge-off and recovery data over a defined historical look-back period. The look-back period represents the number of data periods that will be used to calculate a baseline loss rate for each loan portfolio segment. We determined that the look-back period commencing on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2011 </em>through the current reporting date was reasonable and appropriate, which was used in the calculation of both the <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, allowance for credit losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">Our historical loss rate is then applied to future loan balances at the instrument level based on remaining contractual life adjusted for amortization, prepayment and default to develop a baseline lifetime loss. Our prepayment speed assumptions are developed at the loan segment level based upon the consideration of all relevant data&#160;which we believe could&#160;impact anticipated customer behavior, including changes in interest rates, economic conditions, and underlying property valuations. For the commercial portfolio segments, we assumed a <ix:nonFraction id="c143706342" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-CommercialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivablesPrepaymentSpeedAssumed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2.0</ix:nonFraction>% prepayment speed as of both <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, as we deemed there to be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> considerable changes from historical experience. For the retail <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> family mortgage and retail other consumer portfolios, we used a prepayment speed of <ix:nonFraction id="c143706347" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-RetailPortfolioSegmentMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-OneToFourFamilyMortgagesMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivablesPrepaymentSpeedAssumed" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">9.5</ix:nonFraction>% as of both&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><br/> During each reporting period, we also consider the need to adjust the historical loss rates as determined to reflect the extent to which we expect current conditions and reasonable and supportable economic forecasts to differ from the conditions that existed for the period over which the historical loss information was determined. These qualitative adjustments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>increase or decrease our estimate of expected future credit losses. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we used a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year reasonable and supportable economic forecast period, with a <em style="font: inherit;">six</em>-month straight-line reversion period for all loan segments. The economic forecasts used for our <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, allowance calculation reflected a $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706353" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossPeriodIncreaseDecreaseFromForecastChanges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million allowance balance reduction. The forecasts used for our <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, allowance calculation reflected a $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706354" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="mbwm:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossPeriodIncreaseDecreaseFromForecastChanges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">0.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million allowance balance reduction.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">The allowance for PSL and PCD loans acquired from the acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation&#160;and its wholly owned banking subsidiary, Eastern Michigan Bank, was measured at the loan segment level using proxy expected lifetime loss rates adjusted for qualitative risk factors, including lending management experience, loan review and audit results, asset quality and portfolio trends, loan portfolio growth, industry concentrations, trends in underlying collateral, external factors, and economic conditions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already captured.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-indent: 0pt;">Individual loans exhibiting unique risk characteristics, which differentiated the loans from other loans within the loan segments and were&#160;evaluated for expected credit losses on an individual basis, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706356" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">6.8</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143706357" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.9</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Depreciation expense totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c143707893" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143707894" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Depreciation" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million during the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarters of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">We enter into facility leases in the normal course of business. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, we were under lease contracts for <em style="font: inherit;">eleven</em>&#160;of our banking facilities. The leases have maturity dates ranging from <em style="font: inherit;"> August, 2026 </em>through <em style="font: inherit;"> May, 2048, </em>with a weighted average life of&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageRemainingLeaseTerm1" id="c143707899" format="ixt-sec:duryear">9.4</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. All of our leases have multiple <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143707900">three</span>- to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143707901">five</span>-year extensions; however, these were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> factored in the lease maturities and weighted average lease term as it was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reasonably certain we would exercise the options on the dates we entered into the lease agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Leases are classified as either operating or finance leases at the lease commencement date, with all of our current leases determined to be operating leases. Lease expense for operating leases is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Right-of-use assets represent our right to use&#160;underlying assets for the lease terms, while lease liabilities represent our obligation to make lease payments arising from the leases. Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities are recognized at the lease commencement date at the estimated present value of lease payments over the lease term. We use our incremental borrowing rate, on a collateralized basis, at lease commencement to calculate the present value of lease payments. The weighted average discount rate for leases was <ix:nonFraction id="c143707904" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">6.52</ix:nonFraction>% as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">The right-of-use assets, included in premises and equipment, net on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, and the lease liabilities, included in other liabilities on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c143707909" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143707911" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.9</ix:nonFraction> million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively. As permitted by applicable accounting standards, we have elected <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to recognize short-term leases with original terms of <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months or less on our Consolidated Balance Sheets.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Repurchase agreements have maturities of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c143708031">one</span> business day. Repurchase agreements are treated as financings, and the obligations to repurchase securities sold are reflected as liabilities on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Repurchase agreements are secured by U.S. Government agency securities with an aggregate fair value equal to the aggregate outstanding balance of the repurchase agreements. The securities, which are included in securities available for sale on our Consolidated Balance Sheets, are held in safekeeping by a correspondent bank.</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

The term note bears interest at an annual rate equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c143708079" contextRef="i_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.70</ix:nonFraction>% plus the greater of (a) <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> percent (<ix:nonFraction id="c143708081" contextRef="d_2025-12-24_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">0.0</ix:nonFraction>%) and (b) the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-month forward-looking term rate based on SOFR. Principal shall be paid in quarterly installments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708083" contextRef="d_2025-12-24_2025-12-24_DebtInstrumentAxis-TermNoteMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentPeriodicPaymentPrincipal" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million each.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">8.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<span style="text-decoration: underline; "><b>STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION</b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 18pt; text-align: justify;">
     Stock-based compensation plans are used to provide directors and employees with an increased incentive to contribute to our long-term performance and growth, to align the interests of directors and employees with the interests of our shareholders through the opportunity for increased stock ownership and to attract and retain directors and employees.&#160;Stock-based compensation expense, reported as noninterest expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income,&#160;totaled
    $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708103" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction> million and
    $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708104" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction> million during the&#160;
    <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, respectively.&#160;&#160;
   </div>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 18pt; text-align: justify;">
     &#160;
   </div>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 18pt; text-align: justify;">
     The Stock Incentive Plan of
    <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>&#160;was approved by shareholders in
    <em style="font: inherit;"> May, 2020, </em>and&#160;was effectively replaced with the Stock Incentive Plan of
    <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> that was approved by shareholders in
    <em style="font: inherit;"> May, 2023. </em>Under the Stock Incentive Plans of
    <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> and
    <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> incentive awards
    <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include, but are
    <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, stock options, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights and stock awards. Price, vesting and expiration date parameters are determined by Mercantile&#8217;s Compensation Committee on a grant-by-grant basis.&#160;
    <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> payments are required from employees for restricted stock awards.&#160; The restricted stock awards granted through the plan&#160;fully vest after
    <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> years and, in the case of performance-based restricted stock issued to executive officers issued under the plan, are subject to the attainment of pre-determined performance goals.&#160;
   </div>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">A summary of restricted stock activity during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>,&#160;is as follows:</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsContingenciesAndGuaranteesTextBlock" id="c3166320" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">9.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">COMMITMENTS AND OFF-BALANCE SHEET RISK</span></b><b> </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">We are a party to financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of our customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit. Loan commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Standby letters of credit are conditional commitments issued by our banks to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of a fee. Since many of the commitments are expected to expire without being drawn upon, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amount recognized, if any, in the balance sheet. Our maximum exposure to loan loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instrument for commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit is represented by the contractual notional amount of those instruments. We use the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as we do for on-balance sheet instruments. Collateral, such as accounts receivable, securities, inventory, and property and equipment, is generally obtained based on management&#8217;s credit assessment of the borrower.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">We are required to consider expected credit losses associated with loan commitments over the contractual period in which we are exposed to credit risk on the underlying commitments unless the obligation is unconditionally cancellable by us. Any allowance for off-balance sheet credit exposures is reported as an other liability on our Consolidated Balance Sheets and is increased or decreased via other noninterest expense on our Consolidated Statements of Income. The calculation includes consideration of the likelihood that funding will occur and forecasted credit losses on commitments expected to be funded over their estimated lives. The allowance is calculated using the same aggregate reserve rates calculated for the funded portion of loans at the portfolio level applied to the amount of commitments expected to be funded.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">For commercial lines of credit, retail lines of credit and credit card average outstanding balances, we determined allowance requirements by calculating the difference between the average percent outstanding of the funded commitments over the past several years to actual percent outstanding at the end of the period and applying the respective expected loss allocation factors to the difference as this difference represents the average of unfunded commitments we expect to eventually be drawn upon. For commitments to make loans, we determine an allowance by applying the expected loss allocation factor to the amount expected to be funded. The calculated allowance aggregated $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708167" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RetailAndCommercialLinesOfCreditAndCreditCardReceivablesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708168" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RetailAndCommercialLinesOfCreditAndCreditCardReceivablesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, respectively. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reserve for residential mortgage construction loans, as the loans are for <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year or less and draws are governed by the receipt and satisfactory review of contractor and subcontractor sworn statements, lien waivers and title insurance company endorsements.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">10.</em>&#160;</b>&#160;&#160;<b> </b><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">DERIVATIVES AND HEDGING ACTIVITIES</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">We are exposed to certain risks arising from both business operations and economic conditions. We principally manage the exposure to a wide variety of operational risks through core business activities. Economic risks, including interest rate, liquidity and credit risk, are primarily administered via the amount, sources and duration of assets and liabilities. Derivative financial instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also be used to assist in managing economic risks.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedges are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> speculative and result from a service provided to certain commercial loan borrowers. We execute interest rate swaps with commercial banking customers desiring longer-term fixed rate loans, while simultaneously entering into interest rate swaps with correspondent banks to offset the impact of the interest rate swaps with the commercial banking customers. The net result is the desired floating rate loans and a minimization of the risk exposure of the interest rate swap transactions. As the interest rate swaps associated with this program do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the strict hedge accounting requirements, changes in the fair value of both the commercial banking customer interest rate swaps and the offsetting interest rate swaps with the correspondent banks are recognized directly to earnings. Fees paid to us by the correspondent banks are recognized as noninterest income on our Consolidated Statements of Income on the settlement dates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">The fair values of derivative instruments are reflected in the following table.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">See Note <em style="font: inherit;">12</em>&#160;for a description of the fair value hierarchy as well as a disclosure of levels for classes of financial assets and liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">(<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)</p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size: 10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">It is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practical to determine the fair value of FHLBI stock due to transferability restrictions; therefore, fair value is estimated at carrying amount.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Carrying amount is the estimated fair value for cash and cash equivalents, FHLBI stock, accrued interest receivable and payable, noninterest-bearing checking accounts and securities sold under agreements to repurchase. Security fair values are based on market prices or dealer quotes, and if <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> such information is available, on the rate and term of the security and information about the issuer. Fair value for loans is based on an exit price model as required by ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01,</em> taking into account inputs such as discounted cash flows, probability of default and loss given default assumptions. The fair value for deposit accounts other than noninterest-bearing checking accounts is based on discounted cash flows using current market rates applied to the estimated life. The fair values of subordinated debentures, subordinated notes, and FHLBI advances are based on current rates for similar financing. The fair values of interest rate swaps are based on discounted cash flows using forecasted yield curves, along with insignificant unobservable inputs, such as borrower credit spreads. The fair value of other off-balance sheet items is estimated to be nominal.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. A fair value measurement assumes that the transaction to sell the asset or transfer the liability occurs in the principal market for the asset or liability, or in the absence of a principal market, the most advantageous market for the asset or liability. The price of the principal (or most advantageous) market used to measure the fair value of the asset or liability is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> adjusted for transaction costs. An orderly transaction is a transaction that assumes exposure to the market for a period prior to the measurement date to allow for marketing activities that are usual and customary for transactions involving such assets and liabilities; it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a forced transaction. Market participants are buyers and sellers in the principal market that are (i) independent, (ii) knowledgeable, (iii) able to transact and (iv) willing to transact.</p>
   <ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"></p> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
    <hr style="height: 1px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; width: 100%; border: none; margin: 3pt 0"/> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;">(Continued)</p> <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: center;">&#160;</p></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: center;"></p>

     <div class="hf-row">

        NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
      </div>

     <div class="hf-row">

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementInputsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3166327" escape="true">
   <hr style="height: 1px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; width: 100%; border: none; margin: 3pt 0"/>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">12.</em></b>&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">FAIR VALUES</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">We are required to use valuation techniques that are consistent with the market approach, the income approach and/or the cost approach. The market approach uses prices and other relevant information generated by market transactions involving identical or comparable assets and liabilities. The income approach uses valuation techniques to convert future amounts, such as cash flows or earnings, to a single present amount on a discounted basis. The cost approach is based on the amount that currently would be required to replace the service capacity of an asset (replacement cost). Valuation techniques should be consistently applied. Inputs to valuation techniques refer to the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability. Inputs <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be observable, meaning those that reflect the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability based on market data obtained from independent sources, or unobservable, meaning those that reflect our own assumptions about the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability based on the best information available in the circumstances. In that regard, we utilize a fair value hierarchy for valuation inputs that gives the highest priority to quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The fair value hierarchy is as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets that we have the ability to access as of the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Significant other observable inputs other than Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets; quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active; or other inputs that are observable or can be derived from or corroborated by observable market data by correlation or other means.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Significant unobservable inputs that reflect our own conclusions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">The following is a description of our valuation methodologies used to measure and disclose the fair values of our financial assets and liabilities that are recorded at fair value on a recurring or nonrecurring basis:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Securities available for sale.</i> Securities available for sale are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. Fair value measurement is based on quoted prices, if available. If quoted prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are measured using independent pricing models. Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities include U.S. Government agency debt obligations, mortgage-backed securities issued or guaranteed by U.S. Government agencies, and municipal general obligation and revenue bonds. Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities include bonds issued by certain relatively small municipalities located within our markets that have very limited marketability due to their size and lack of ratings from a recognized rating service. We carry these bonds at historical cost, which we believe approximates fair value, unless our periodic financial analysis or other information that becomes known to us necessitates an impairment. There was <ix:nonFraction id="c143708375" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_InformationByCategoryOfDebtSecurityAxis-AvailableforsaleSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ValuationAllowancesAndReservesBalance" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> such impairment as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, or <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>. We have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> securities available for sale.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Derivatives</i>. We measure fair value utilizing models that use primarily market observable inputs, such as forecasted yield curves. Insignificant unobservable inputs, such as borrower credit spreads, are also utilized.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Mortgage loans held for sale</i>. Mortgage loans originated and intended for sale in the secondary market are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or market, as determined by outstanding commitments from investors, and are measured on a nonrecurring basis. Fair value is based on independent quoted market prices, where applicable, or the prices for other mortgage whole loans with similar characteristics. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, we determined the fair value of our mortgage loans held for sale to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708380" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MortgagesHeldForSaleFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">21.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c143708381" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:MortgagesHeldForSaleFairValueDisclosure" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">17.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Loans</i>. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> record loans at fair value on a recurring basis. However, from time to time, we record nonrecurring fair value adjustments to collateral dependent loans to reflect partial write-downs or specific reserves that are based on the observable market price or current estimated value of the collateral. These loans are reported in the nonrecurring table below at initial recognition of significant borrower distress and on an ongoing basis until recovery or charge-off. The fair values of distressed loans are determined using either the sales comparison approach or income approach; respective unobservable inputs for the approaches consist of adjustments for differences between comparable sales and the utilization of appropriate capitalization rates.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"><i>Foreclosed Assets. </i>At time of foreclosure or repossession, foreclosed and repossessed assets are adjusted to fair value less costs to sell upon transfer of the loans to foreclosed and repossessed assets, establishing a new cost basis. We subsequently adjust estimated fair value of foreclosed assets on a nonrecurring basis to reflect write-downs based on revised fair value estimates. The fair values of parcels of other real estate owned are determined using either the sales comparison approach or income approach; respective unobservable inputs for the approaches consist of adjustments for differences between comparable sales and the utilization of appropriate capitalization rates.</p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: center; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <hr style="height: 1px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; width: 100%; border: none; margin: 3pt 0"/>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: center; margin: 0pt;">(Continued)</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: center; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt; text-align: justify;">The carrying values are based on the estimated value of the property or other assets. Fair value estimates of collateral on nonperforming loans and foreclosed assets are reviewed periodically. Our credit policies establish criteria for obtaining appraisals and determining internal value estimates. We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also adjust outside appraisals and internal evaluations based on identifiable trends within our markets, such as sales of similar properties or assets, listing prices and offers received. In addition, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>discount certain appraised and internal value estimates to address current distressed market conditions. We generally assign a discount factor range of <ix:nonFraction id="c143708391" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_CollateralAxis-CommercialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c143708392" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_CollateralAxis-CommercialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">60</ix:nonFraction>% for commercial real estate dependent loans and foreclosed assets, and a discount factor range of <ix:nonFraction id="c143708393" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_CollateralAxis-ResidentialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">25</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c143708394" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_CollateralAxis-ResidentialRealEstateMember_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">50</ix:nonFraction>% for residential-related properties. In a vast majority of cases, we assign a <ix:nonFraction id="c143708395" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_FinancingReceivableRecordedInvestmentByClassOfFinancingReceivableAxis-RealEstateDependentLoansAndForeclosedAssetsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="mbwm:FairValueInputsDiscountFactor" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="1">10</ix:nonFraction>% discount factor for estimated selling costs.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em></b>&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>Mercantile completed its acquisition of Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation&#160;and its wholly owned banking subsidiary, Eastern Michigan Bank, in accordance with the Agreement and Plan of Merger, as amended (the "Merger Agreement") by and between Mercantile, Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation, and Shamrock Merger Sub LLC, a wholly owned special purpose subsidiary of Mercantile (&#8220;Merger Sub&#8221;), entered into on <em style="font: inherit;"> July 22, 2025. </em>Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation merged with and into Merger Sub, with Merger Sub continuing as the surviving entity (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;). Immediately following the Merger, and also effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>Merger Sub merged with and into Mercantile, with Mercantile continuing as the surviving entity. The newly acquired Eastern Michigan Bank will operate alongside Mercantile Bank until the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2027,</em> at which time Mercantile plans to consolidate Eastern Michigan Bank into Mercantile Bank.</p>

    <hr style="height: 1px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; width: 100%; border: none; margin: 3pt 0"/> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">13.</em></b>&#160;&#160;<b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">BUSINESS COMBINATIONS</span>&#160;</b>(continued)</p></ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 17pt; text-align: justify;">Mercantile accounted for the Eastern Michigan Financial Corporation acquisition as a business combination using the acquisition method of accounting in accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> Business Combinations ("ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805"</em>). ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805</em> requires assets purchased and liabilities assumed to be recorded at their respective fair values as of the date of acquisition. Mercantile determined the fair value of loans, core deposit intangibles, mortgage servicing rights, time deposits, and real property with the assistance of <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations and appraisals.
